# L-001: G. J. Wirsching, "The Dynamical System Generated by the 3n+1 Function"

Springer Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1681, 1998. Verified against the primary source PDF
(archived at `/home/rat/Google/Projetos/Claude/ResearchOS/projects/collatz/literature/papers/131_Dynamical-System-3n1-Function-Wirsching-Book.pdf`, not copied into this repo: it is
the full copyrighted book, 10.7MB, not something to commit to a public repository).

## Verified definitions (checked 2026-07-22, pdftotext extraction against the actual pages)

**Corollary & Notation 1.8** (Chapter V, Section 1, p.127; introduced informally already in
the book's Introduction, p.4-5):

```
R_{j,k} := { sum_{i=0}^{j} 2^{a_i} 3^i : j+k >= a_0 > a_1 > ... > a_j >= 0 }
|R_{j,k}| = C(j+k+1, j+1)
```

Matches exactly what the researcher's brief and the previous paper's main.tex (line 1171-1173)
state. One small citation-labeling note: the previous project's H-114 note and this project's
initial brief cite this as "Corollary II.5.8"; the primary source PDF actually labels it
"Corollary & Notation 1.8" within Chapter V (page 127 is correct in both). Not chasing this
further, it does not affect the mathematical content, only an internal cross-reference label.

**Conjecture 3.8 (strong form, p.138, "Covering Conjecture for Mixed Power Sums")**: exists
constant K>0 (not depending on j or l) such that |R_{j-1,j}| >= K*2*3^{l-1} implies R_{j-1,j}
covers Z_3^* mod 3^l.

**Conjecture 3.9 (weak form, p.139, "Weak Covering Conjecture for Mixed Power Sums")**, verbatim
confirmed against the PDF:

```
Suppose K(l) > 0 is a function growing less than an exponential,
    lim_{l->inf} K(l) e^{-gamma*l} = 0   for any constant gamma > 0.
Then, for every j, l in N, the following implication holds:
    |R_{j-1,j}| >= K(l) * 3^l   =>   R_{j-1,j} covers Z_3^* modulo 3^l.
```

Matches the researcher's brief and HYPOTHESES.md H-001 exactly. This is the conjecture this
project extends computationally.

**Reduction Theorem 3.10**: if the weak covering conjecture holds, then
`liminf_x (inf_{a in N\3N} Z_a(delta*x)/x) > 0` for any delta in (0,1), i.e. uniform
sub-positive predecessor density for the 3x+1 map. This is the actual payoff Wirsching derives
from Conjecture 3.9; the proof (p.139-140) uses the expansion factor
`|R_{j-1,j}|/|R_{j-2,j-1}| = C(2j,j)/C(2j-2,j-1) -> 4` and the standard binomial asymptotic
`C(2j,j) ~ 4^j/sqrt(pi*j)`, which is exactly where the threshold log_4(3) in e(l) comes from.

## Back-tracing formalism and the R_{j,k}/F_{j,k} identity (read 2026-07-28, Chapter II Sec. 2 and Chapter V Sec. 1)

**Chapter II, Section 2** (pp.38-42) defines the back-tracing machinery cited secondhand by
Monks et al. (L-009) and used in `notes/H-004.md`. A feasible vector `s=(s_0,...,s_k) in F` has
length `l(s):=k` (not k+1, despite k+1 components) and back-tracing operator `v_s`, composing
inverse Collatz moves. Definition 1.4/Lemma 1.7 (p.126-127) define a normalized remainder map
`R: F -> Z_3^*` with the key uniqueness property (Lemma 3.1, p.45): for `s in F` there is exactly
one residue class `a mod 3^{l(s)}` such that `s` is admissible w.r.t. `b` iff `b == a mod 3^{l(s)}`.

**Chapter V, Corollary & Notation 1.8, p.127** (same numbered result already cited in this note
for R_{j,k}'s definition) states, verbatim confirmed against the actual page image (not just
OCR text, which was unreliable enough on this page to need the visual check):

```
F_{j,k} := {s=(s_0,...,s_j) in F : l(s)=j, |s|=k}
R_{j,k} := {sum_{i=0}^{j} 2^{a_i}3^i : j+k >= a_0>a_1>...>a_j>=0}
Then  R_{j,k} = R(F_{j+1,k})   and   |R_{j,k}| = C(j+k+1, j+1)
```

This is an exact SET EQUALITY (not just equal cardinality): Wirsching's own R_{j,k} (the mixed
power sum set this project's j*(l) is built from) equals the normalized-remainder image of
F_{j+1,k}, feasible back-tracing vectors of length j+1. The proof gives an explicit bijection
formula between the index tuple (a_0,...,a_j) and s in F_{j+1,k}.

**Independently re-verified numerically** (not taken on the book's word, per this project's
honesty rules): implemented both the raw sum and the R(s) normalized-remainder formula (the
correct one, `alpha_i := (l-1-i) + s_0+...+s_{l-1-i}`, read directly off a rendered page image
after an initial OCR-text transcription attempt gave a formula that only matched 4 of 6 test
cases and was discarded as unreliable) for R_{1,2} (l=2 case matching this project's own
verified l=2,j=2 baseline). All 6 valid index tuples gave an exact match between the raw sum and
R(s), and the resulting residue set was exactly `{1,2,5,7} mod 9`, matching the project's
existing checkpoint exactly. See `notes/H-004.md` for what this resolves.

**Also found, flagged as context not yet a usable bound**: Definition 1.2/1.12 and Lemma 1.13
(pp.125-129) define "(j,k,l)-locally/globally covering triples": whether `{v_s(a): s in
E_{j,k}(a)}` covers Z_3^* modulo `3^{l-j}`, for vector-length `j` STRICTLY LESS than the target
modulus exponent `l` (`j<l` required throughout). Combined with the R_{j,k}=R(F_{j+1,k}) identity
above: this project's own j*(l) question is the degenerate case `j=l` (vector length equals the
target modulus exponent exactly), which sits right at the boundary of what Wirsching's own
recursive covering machinery (Lemma 1.3's inductive step relating `e_l` to `e_{l-j}`) was built
for (`j<l`, strictly shorter vectors covering a finer modulus). This is a plausible structural
explanation for part of why j*(l) is hard: it is precisely the boundary case Wirsching's own
1998 apparatus does not directly reach, not a case his book already handles and this project
missed. Not pursued further here (would need working through whether Lemma 1.3's estimate says
anything nontrivial as `j -> l`); flagged for H-003 as new context, see `notes/H-003.md`.
